title: Biotechnology
tagline: Recombinant DNA, protein production, genome editing, synthetic circuits, metabolic engineering, bioprocessing, agricultural biotechnology and biosafety
summary: Biotechnology uses living systems to make products and solve problems, and synthetic biology tries to make that engineering predictable. This course covers recombinant DNA and protein production, genome editing with CRISPR and related tools, the design of genetic circuits, metabolic engineering, scaling up in bioprocesses, agricultural biotechnology, and the biosafety, biosecurity and ethical questions that these powers raise.

chapters.title: Recombinant DNA technology
chapters.summary: Vectors and hosts, and the design of DNA constructs from restriction cloning to DNA synthesis.

chapters.title: Producing proteins
chapters.summary: Expression in bacteria, yeast and mammalian cells, and protein engineering.

chapters.title: Genome editing
chapters.summary: Zinc fingers, TALENs and CRISPR–Cas systems, base and prime editing, and their accuracy and limits.

chapters.title: Synthetic biology
chapters.summary: Standard parts, genetic circuits, biosensors and the design–build–test cycle.

chapters.title: Metabolic engineering
chapters.summary: Engineering microbes to make fuels, chemicals and medicines.

chapters.title: Bioprocess engineering
chapters.summary: Bioreactors, growth and production kinetics at scale, and downstream processing.

chapters.title: Plant and agricultural biotechnology
chapters.summary: Transgenic and genome-edited crops, their traits and how they are regulated.

chapters.title: Biosafety, biosecurity and ethics
chapters.summary: Containment, dual-use research, regulation and the ethics of modifying living things.
